domain_restrictions: for each i in 1..d, w_i is a positive integer
S is graded so that each x_i has degree w_i (and grading is compatible with polynomial multiplication)
R is positively graded, meaning it decomposes as direct sum over n >= 0 of R_n
Hilbert series coefficients use dim_k R_n, so each R_n is finite-dimensional as a k-vector space in the intended setting (implicitly required for the series to make sense as stated)
each g_i is homogeneous with respect to the given grading on S
g_1,...,g_d is a regular sequence in S of length exactly d
for each i in 1..d, e_i is the degree of g_i and therefore is compatible with the grading (typically a positive integer, though nonnegative is not explicitly excluded)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Fix a field k, a nonnegative integer d, and positive integers w_1 through w_d. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring k[x_1,...,x_d] with deg(x_i)=w_i. If g_1 through g_d are homogeneous elements forming a regular sequence in S and e_i=deg(g_i) for each i, then the Hilbert series of the graded quotient S modulo the ideal generated by g_1 through g_d satisfies Hilb of S/(g_1,...,g_d) at q equals the product over i=1..d of (1 - q to the e_i) divided by the product over i=1..d of (1 - q to the w_i), with the convention that when d=0 both products are empty and evaluate to 1.

statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. For a positively graded k-algebra R = direct_sum_{n >= 0} R_n, write Hilb_R(q) := sum_{n >= 0} (dim_k R_n) q^n. If g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S and deg(g_i)=e_i for each i, then Hilb_{S/(g_1,...,g_d)}(q) = prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(e_i)) / prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(w_i)), with the empty product interpreted as 1 when d=0.
